text:
The evidence can't tell you that. It shows tree-cover loss, not a rule violation.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022 inside ASSET-I (3.41% of the 17.6 ha property). The JRC 2020 map agrees that the area was forest, and later years of data were observed, so the loss is corroborated. The MGAP 2021 map places about 0.5 ha of the area in native forest and 0.1 ha outside mapped forest. None of it is planted forest. A further 0.2 ha of loss was in patches too small to count as an event.

What it does not establish: whether deforestation or land-use change occurred, the cause (harvest, fire, storm, clearing), whether the change was legal or authorized, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.

To judge a violation, you would need permits or authorizations, the applicable native forest rules, and field or higher-resolution evidence on cause and land use afterward.
